title: Market Organization and Structure
overview: Market structure explains how assets, intermediaries, orders, positions, leverage, and settlement fit together.
example: Turn a business or market assumption into a forecast, required return, and valuation implication.

modules.title: Markets, Assets, and Intermediaries
modules.explanation: Market organization connects issuers, investors, intermediaries, venues, orders, clearing, and settlement. Position direction and leverage determine exposure, while order instructions trade execution certainty against price control.
steps: Identify the asset, venue, counterparty, and settlement process.
Translate long, short, or leveraged positions into payoff and loss exposure.
Choose order type and validity based on urgency, liquidity, and price risk.
modules.check: Explain how markets, assets, and intermediaries changes an analyst's conclusion, including one limitation.
objectives: Explain markets, assets, and intermediaries in plain language and connect it to the reading's central problem.
Apply the analytical decision rule or analytical decision rule with clearly labeled inputs.
Interpret the result, challenge its assumptions, and identify one condition that would change the conclusion.
lesson: Market organization connects issuers, investors, intermediaries, venues, orders, clearing, and settlement. Position direction and leverage determine exposure, while order instructions trade execution certainty against price control.

Equity analysis connects industry structure and company economics with forecasts, required return, and value. A valuation is a conditional result: it is useful when the operating assumptions are explicit and internally consistent.
